# Contributing to fast-check

🐱 First off, thanks for taking the time to contribute! 🐱

The following is a set of guidelines for contributing to fast-check and its packages.
These are mostly guidelines, not rules.
Use your best judgment, and feel free to propose changes to this document in a pull request.

**Feel free to contribute, ask questions, report bugs and issue pull requests**

## Table of Contents

- [How Can I Contribute?](#how-can-i-contribute)
  - [Asking questions](#asking-questions)
  - [Reporting bugs](#reporting-bugs)
  - [Issuing pull requests](#issuing-pull-requests)
    - [Getting started](#getting-started)
    - [Code style](#code-style)
    - [GitHub Actions integration](#github-actions-integration)
    - [Notify how impactful your change will be](#notify-how-impactful-your-change-will-be)
    - [Naming your pull request](#naming-your-pull-request)
    - [Update your PR](#update-your-pr)
    - [Resync PR with main](#resync-pr-with-main)
  - [Examples](#examples)
    - [Adding a new arbitrary](#adding-a-new-arbitrary)
- [Can I use AI?](#can-i-use-ai)

## How Can I Contribute?

### Asking questions

Before asking questions, please double-check you can not find your answer in one of the examples provided or in the documentation of the project:

- [Documentation](https://github.com/dubzzz/fast-check/blob/main/README.md)
- [Examples provided inside the project](https://github.com/dubzzz/fast-check/tree/main/examples)
- [Examples of properties](https://github.com/dubzzz/fast-check-examples)
- [Example: fuzzing a REST API](https://github.com/dubzzz/fuzz-rest-api)

If nothing answered your question, please do not hesitate to [create a new issue in GitHub](https://github.com/dubzzz/fast-check/issues).

### Reporting bugs

You should report bugs using [create a new issue in GitHub](https://github.com/dubzzz/fast-check/issues).

### Issuing pull requests

#### Getting started

In order to start playing with the code locally you must run the following set of commands:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/dubzzz/fast-check.git && cd fast-check
pnpm install
pnpm --filter fast-check build    #compile the code in packages/fast-check/src, build the packages/fast-check/lib content
```

Once done, everything is ready for you to start working on the code.

#### Code style

Code style standard is enforced by Prettier.
Once done with your development you can check it follow the recommended code style by running `pnpm format:check` or run autofixes with `pnpm format`.

You should also check for linting by running `pnpm lint:check` and fix lint problems with `pnpm lint`.

#### GitHub Actions integration

All pull requests will trigger GitHub Actions checks.
It ensures that the pull request follow the code style of the project and do not break existing tests.

#### Notify how impactful your change will be

Any change in the code may have impact in the next release. In order to ease our deployment process we try to anticipate as much as possible the impacts of each single pull request from a semver point of view:

- decline: really no impact code side from a bundle point of view
- patch: no visible impact, generally mostly fixing bugs or typos in the code
- minor: new features
- major: breaking changes

In order to ease this work, before opening the PR (or after if you forgot to do it), you should run the script `pnpm -w run bump` to underline which packages have been impacted. Please note that our internals and private packages must always be toggled to 'decline' as we don't plan to bump their versions.

#### Naming your pull request

We follow the [gitmoji](https://gitmoji.dev/) specification for PR titles. Each PR title must start with a gitmoji that describes the nature of the change. Here are some commonly used ones:

| Gitmoji | Code                    | Description          |
| ------- | ----------------------- | -------------------- |
| ✨      | `:sparkles:`            | New feature          |
| 🐛      | `:bug:`                 | Bug fix              |
| 📝      | `:memo:`                | Documentation        |
| ✅      | `:white_check_mark:`    | Tests                |
| 🏷️      | `:label:`               | Types                |
| ⚡️      | `:zap:`                 | Performance          |
| ♻️      | `:recycle:`             | Refactoring          |
| 🔧      | `:wrench:`              | Configuration        |
| 🎨      | `:art:`                 | Code style/format    |
| 🔥      | `:fire:`                | Remove code/files    |
| ⬆️      | `:arrow_up:`            | Upgrade dependencies |
| 🗑️      | `:wastebasket:`         | Deprecation          |
| 👷      | `:construction_worker:` | CI                   |

For the full list, see [gitmoji.dev](https://gitmoji.dev/).

When the change targets a package **other than `fast-check`**, add the package scope in parentheses after the emoji. The available scopes correspond to the package directory names:

- `ava` — for `@fast-check/ava`
- `jest` — for `@fast-check/jest`
- `vitest` — for `@fast-check/vitest`
- `worker` — for `@fast-check/worker`
- `poisoning` — for `@fast-check/poisoning`
- `packaged` — for `@fast-check/packaged`

**Examples:**

- `✨ Add new arbitrary for dates` — a feature in the main `fast-check` package (no scope needed)
- `🐛(vitest) Fix compatibility with vitest 4` — a bug fix in `@fast-check/vitest`
- `📝(jest) Improve usage examples` — documentation update for `@fast-check/jest`

#### Update your PR

If you plan to update your PR with either a fix for the tests or change following code reviews please directly commit your new commit in your branch, PR will get updated automatically.

Before your fix:

```
--*---> main    on dubzzz/fast-check
   \
   #1   branch-pr on your fork
```

After your fix:

```
--*--->        main    on dubzzz/fast-check
   \
   #1 --- #2   branch-pr on your fork
```

#### Resync PR with main

Ideally to resync your branch with main prefer a merge of main branch into your PR branch. It has the advantage to preserves the commit history on GitHub PR (contrary to rebase and force push).

### Examples

#### Adding a new arbitrary

✔️ _Create a feature request_

Before adding any new arbitrary into fast-check please make sure to fill a `Feature request` to justify the need for such arbitrary.

✔️ _Code the arbitrary_

All the arbitraries defined by fast-check are available in `src/arbitrary`.
Create a new file for the new one if it does not fit into the existing ones.

✔️ _Test the arbitrary_

Most of the newly added arbitraries will just be a combination of existing ones (mostly mapping from one entry to another).
We expect a quite minimal amount of tests to be added as most of the logic depends on the built-in blocks.

- _Unit-test_ & _Integration_ - in `test/unit/arbitrary`

```js
import * as fc from 'fast-check';
import { myArbitrary } from '../../../../src/arbitrary/MyArbitrary';
import {
  assertProduceCorrectValues,
  assertProduceSameValueGivenSameSeed,
  assertProduceValuesShrinkableWithoutContext,
  assertShrinkProducesSameValueWithoutInitialContext,
  assertShrinkProducesStrictlySmallerValue,
} from './__test-helpers__/NextArbitraryAssertions';

describe('myArbitrary', () => {
  // Tests in isolation!
  // You may want to check that generate, canShrinkWithoutContext and shrink
  // are working as expecting given mocked or stubbed data (see our usage of spies).
});

describe('myArbitrary (integration)', () => {
  // Tests in real life!
  // In this section we assess that the arbitrary will work as expected by calling it with a real random generator
  // and without mocking any of its underlyings. In order to do that we have an already predefined set of helpers.
  // Among those helpers only some are really compulsory as they will ensure that the arbitrary does not break the
  // rules. The other ones tend to have the best possible version of the arbitrary by ensuring the shrinker will
  // always shrink towards strictly smaller values or that user defined values can be shrunk.

  type Extra = /* Typing for the extra props received by myArbitraryBuilder */

report.overview: fast-check is a TypeScript property-based testing library for JavaScript and TypeScript developers: users describe input generators and predicates, and the library generates cases, shrinks failures, and reports reproducible seed/path coordinates. At commit ecf7193810d1057253808105444e147d948051a1, the core exposes asyncProperty and promise-returning check/assert APIs, alongside model-based testing, controlled promise scheduling, and execution plugins. The pnpm monorepo also contains Jest, Vitest, and AVA integrations, Node worker execution, packaging and global-poisoning utilities, and a Docusaurus documentation website.
report.agent_prompt:
Onboard to fast-check at commit ecf7193810d1057253808105444e147d948051a1 using repository evidence rather than assumptions about previously released fast-check APIs. This brief comes from bounded, read-only source inspection. Tests and CI were inspected, not executed; their existence does not establish passing results. For a similarly restricted investigation, prefix shell reads with rtk proxy, do not install dependencies, execute repository code, write files, access secrets, or make network calls.

Start with package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, packages/fast-check/package.json, tsconfig.common.json, vitest.config.mjs, and packages/fast-check/src/fast-check.ts. The root uses pnpm 12.5.1, Rolldown builds, Vitest tests, oxfmt formatting, and oxlint linting. The public package manifest exports lib/fast-check.js. Shared build configuration derives source inputs from package exports and generates declarations. Do not infer runtime compatibility from the manifest's Node minimum alone: inspect current source features and CI bundle tests.

Trace the main operation through AsyncProperty.ts, PropertyImplem.ts, Runner.ts, Tosser.ts, SourceValuesIterator.ts, RunnerIterator.ts, RunExecution.ts, and RunDetailsFormatter.ts. asyncProperty combines arbitraries into a tuple. check merges global and local parameters, instantiates plugins, decorates generation and execution, produces examples followed by random cases, awaits predicates sequentially, and switches to shrinking after failure. assert adds reporting. Both check and assert return promises at this commit. Seed and colon-separated counterexamplePath support replay through lazyToss and PathWalker; this is reconstruction from execution coordinates, with state retained in memory by the inspected runner.

For generator work, read Arbitrary.ts, Value.ts, the relevant public arbitrary factory, its internal implementation, and colocated specifications. Preserve generation determinism, shrink context, context-free shrink eligibility, and cloning behavior. Existing ArbitraryAssertions helpers assess seed determinism and other generator invariants. Changes to generation or shrink ordering can affect replay.

For integrations, inspect each package independently. Vitest wraps test/it and adapts tuple versus record properties, reporters, plugins, and suite hooks. Its ordinary test wrapper also provides context.g. Worker properties require the worker package's assert for orchestration and cleanup. Main-thread generation sends values over worker messaging; worker generation sends RNG state and disables shrinking. Worker threads execute supplied files and should not be treated as a security sandbox.

During an authorized implementation task, begin with the smallest relevant Vitest project/file using the root test script with --run; then apply relevant typecheck, formatting, lint, bundle, or documentation checks. These are recommendations, not checks performed by this investigation. Documentation tests can evaluate snippets and write Markdown when UPDATE_CODE_SNIPPETS is enabled. Packaging utilities can recursively delete nonpublished files unless dryRun is selected. Inspect CI publication conditions before touching release tooling, and leave external submission to the human owner in accordance with AI_POLICY.md. Report source observations and hypotheses separately, and reproduce suspected defects before describing them as confirmed.

system_map.summary: The system centers on an importable testing library rather than an application server. Generation, execution, shrinking, and reporting are separate core modules; adapters and worker orchestration form additional runtime boundaries. Builds produce publishable library artifacts and a static documentation site. The inspected runner retains execution state in memory and exposes replay coordinates through its reports.

claims.claim: The workspace includes examples, packages/*, and website; root scripts orchestrate package builds, Vitest tests and benchmarks, parallel typechecking, oxfmt, oxlint, and publication lint.

The core package exports lib/fast-check.js, publishes lib, declares sideEffects:false, and depends on pure-rand; fast-check.ts explicitly exports generators, runner APIs, model runners, scheduler APIs, and plugins.
asyncProperty constructs PropertyImplem around tuple arbitraries; check coordinates parameter qualification, plugin instances, input iteration, predicate execution, and RunExecution reporting.
RunExecution owns counters, failure values, error objects, paths, and optional execution trees in memory; toRunDetails returns those values and the qualified run configuration.
Jest and Vitest export enriched test/it functions, while AVA exports testProp; @fast-check/worker adds a Node worker_threads boundary around predicate execution.

buildConfigFor derives src entrypoints from package exports, emits ESM plus declarations, externalizes bare imports, and emits CJS only for conditional exports; core build metadata uses GITHUB_SHA or a fixed git rev-parse HEAD shell command.
The website is Docusaurus with React pages, autogenerated documentation navigation, Algolia search/Ask AI, offline PWA activation, and TypeDoc-generated API documentation from the core entrypoint.

Build Status gates package publication on required checks and tags at HEAD, publishes npm artifacts with attestations, and contains a disabled Netlify publication job; separate workflows create draft releases, announce on Bluesky, and force-mirror main/tags to Tangled.

feature_catalog.summary: Users primarily consume a programmatic API for generative testing and reproducible failure diagnosis. Generator composition, model commands, and promise scheduling support more complex test scenarios. Plugins and framework adapters customize execution and integration. Companion packages and the documentation website provide additional developer-facing capabilities.

claims.claim: asyncProperty accepts arbitraries and a synchronous or asynchronous predicate; check returns RunDetails, while assert reports failure through a rejected promise by default.
The public generator catalog includes numbers, strings, dates, functions, collections, recursive structures, JSON, entity graphs, network-shaped strings, identifiers, and typed arrays.
sample materializes generated values; statistics classifies values into one or more categories, sorts category counts, and emits percentage lines through the configured logger.

modelRun and asyncModelRun execute commands conditionally against model/real pairs; scheduledModelRun combines commands with a scheduler that also supports promises, functions, sequences, waiting, and task reports.

Execution options include seed, randomType, numRuns, examples, replay path, skip tolerance, verbosity, and endOnFailure; public plugins add lifecycle hooks, unbiased generation, equal-value handling, interruption, and predicate timeouts.

Vitest .prop supports tuple or record arbitraries and forwards test modifiers; ordinary wrapped Vitest tests receive context.g. Jest exposes enriched test/it, and AVA testProp exposes only, failing, skip, serial, before, and after.

Worker properties select file/property/predicate isolation and main-thread/worker generation; poisoning utilities detect or restore global changes, and packaged utilities list published files or remove nonpublished content.
The documentation surface offers Quick Start, tutorials, API reference, blog, search, and support navigation; the homepage leads to a Vitest tutorial scaffold containing sort.mjs and sort.test.mjs.

data_flow.summary: Input data enters through arbitrary factories, predicates, and execution parameters. Generated values carry shrink context, while runner-owned state records execution outcomes and replay coordinates. Plugins transform generation and predicate execution before results reach reporting. Worker execution introduces message serialization or RNG-state reconstruction as an additional boundary.

claims.claim: asyncProperty splits its arguments into arbitraries and predicate, wraps each arbitrary in AlwaysShrinkableArbitrary, and converts the resulting tuple into positional predicate arguments.

check overlays local parameters on readConfigureGlobal; qualification defaults to 100 runs, 100 skips per run, empty examples/path, and xorshift128plus, normalizing supplied seeds to a 32-bit representation.
Each check creates a symbol-keyed plugin Map; global plugin builders precede local builders, and reverse-order decoration makes earlier plugins wrap later generation/run behavior.

toss yields supplied examples before random cases, jumping the RNG before each generated case; PropertyImplem converts run IDs to bias frequency and protects undefined shrink context with a placeholder.
Value stores value_ and context and optionally exposes clone-aware value access; RunnerIterator passes value_ to the predicate and retains the associated Value for subsequent shrinking.

Predicate true/undefined becomes success, thrown PreconditionFailure becomes skip/interruption, and other errors become PropertyFailure; failed outcomes replace the active iterator with shrinks, while skips replenish the initial-run budget.

RunExecution converts accumulated state into RunDetails containing seed, counterexamplePath, errorInstance, and configuration; assert then calls a custom reporter or formats the counterexample, shrink count, and reproduction parameters.

Worker mode sends either generated inputs or rngState/runId payloads with predicate and run identifiers; workers reconstruct inputs when needed and return success, failure, or skipped messages, which BasicPool correlates to the current registration.

behavior_traces.summary: Source reads followed ordinary assertion, failure replay, worker-backed assertion, and framework registration through their output boundaries. Additional traces cover sampling, model commands, scheduler release, and website onboarding. These are execution-order reconstructions from source, not observed runtime results. The replay flow reconstructs a failure from seed/path rather than loading persisted execution objects.

claims.claim: Assertion flow: asyncProperty → PropertyImplem(tuple(...)) → assert → check → read(parameters) → plugin construction/decoration → toss → SourceValuesIterator → runIt → RunnerIterator; runIt awaits each predicate and feeds its result back before advancing.

Failure flow: PropertyImplem.run converts an error/false result → RunnerIterator.handleResult calls RunExecution.fail → the iterator switches to property.shrink → each further failure extends the path; endOnFailure substitutes an empty shrink iterator before execution.

Replay flow: check with a nonempty path → lazyToss → pathWalk parses colon-separated indices → drops initial producers → generates the selected value → repeatedly shrinks and drops candidates → ordinary execution; RunExecution.mergePaths incorporates the starting offset.

Worker flow: propertyFor → workerProperty → runMainThread selects a pool/builds the property → worker assert injects the worker plugin → beforeEach acquires a lock and worker → register/postMessage → runWorker executes the predicate → response resolves the run → assert finally invokes associated pool cleanup; file-scoped pools may defer actual worker termination.

Vitest .prop flow: buildTest exposes .prop → buildTestProp selects tuple or record conversion → buildTestWithPropRunner selects a seed and creates asyncProperty → registered callback collects suite hooks and adds lifecycle plugins → awaited fc.assert executes the property.

Sampling flow: sample → streamSample merges parameters → toProperty wraps the input → toss or replay pathWalk → take(numRuns) → value_ extraction → array materialization; statistics consumes that stream and emits sorted category percentages.

Model/scheduler flow: asyncModelRun → internalAsyncModelRun → setup → genericModelRun chains commands → await command.check → conditionally await command.run; scheduledModelRun wraps commands, schedules startModel, then waits for the model and all remaining scheduler tasks.

Website onboarding flow: Home renders HomepageHeader and feature content → Quick Start links to basic-setup → the guide scaffolds a tutorial with degit → identifies sort.mjs/sort.test.mjs and Vitest → instructs npm test; homepage example demonstrates awaited assert(asyncProperty(...)).

testing_signals.summary: Tests and CI were inspected, not executed; no passing result or coverage percentage is asserted. Vitest discovers tests across packages, examples, and website, with both colocated specifications and package-level integration suites. The inspected tests address execution, replay, generator invariants, scheduler behavior, worker timeouts, and adapter subprocess integration. Coverage configuration and documentation filters impose explicit limits, and this inventory is bounded rather than exhaustive.

claims.claim: Root Vitest configuration discovers test/spec files across workspace projects, excludes test-bundle, .test-artifacts, and tutorial templates, sets a 120-second timeout, and scopes coverage to core source.

Colocated Runner.spec.ts checks default run counts, generation/execution ordering, endOnFailure, replay-before-shrink-suppression, rejected assertions, reproduction messages, and original-error causes.

ReplayFailures integration tests reconstruct counterexamples with sample(seed,path), rebuild shrink-path prefixes, replay the minimal failure, test endOnFailure behavior, and reject impossible replay paths.

ArbitraryAssertions uses fast-check itself to compare generated and shrunk values from identical seeds; an afterEach plugin checks global poisoning and attempts restoration before rethrowing a detected change.

Scheduler specifications use Vitest mocks and controlled unresolved promises to check empty-queue errors, task selection, act wrapping, and waiting; worker E2E tests assert a timeout for a predicate that blocks its worker event loop.

Vitest adapter integration tests generate isolated specification/config files, invoke a child Node/Vitest process, and inspect textual pass/fail/skip markers; child environments remove listed agent variables to preserve reporter output.

Documentation tests scan core-block arbitrary Markdown, evaluate selected snippets, compare regenerated content, and optionally write updates; SKIP_DOCUMENTATION bypasses them, and Unicode examples explicitly depend on the runtime's Unicode version.

CI defines sharded Linux tests on Node 22/24/latest and macOS/Windows tests on Node 24, enables coverage on macOS, and separately checks packaged bundles and TypeScript latest/5.8 fixtures; configured core-only coverage does not quantify adapter or website coverage.

risk_map.summary: These risks are source observations or explicitly labeled hypotheses, not confirmed vulnerabilities. The main runtime sensitivities are nonterminating generation, user-controlled execution, cleanup ordering, and compatibility assumptions. Filesystem deletion and release automation require separate operational caution. Partial inspection does not establish whole-repository absence of authentication, network activity, tests, or other safeguards.

claims.claim: FilterArbitrary.generate retries synchronously without a retry bound; timeout decorates predicate execution, cannot stop a running predicate, and has no effect on synchronous execution. An always-rejecting generator can therefore stall before predicate timeout handling.

Worker execution loads a supplied file URL through new Worker without sandbox restrictions in that constructor; main-thread inputs must cross messaging serialization, worker-generated inputs disable shrinking, and package documentation requires its own assert to avoid lingering workers.

Hypothesis: terminateIfStillRunning searches for w.worker !== worker before splicing, which appears capable of removing another pooled worker or the last entry when no unequal worker exists. Reproduction is needed before calling this a confirmed cleanup defect.

Completion hooks are attached with runDetailsPromise.then rather than a rejection handler/finally; all hooks are attempted after a resolved RunDetails, but that implementation does not provide the same cleanup path when the run promise rejects before producing details.

removeNonPublishedFiles accepts a caller-supplied packageRoot, normalizes it, and recursively removes excluded children; dryRun defaults to false and normalized relative child paths are compared against the caller-supplied keep strings, making an incorrect root operationally consequential.

Global parameters are held and returned by reference, while installed global plugins append to a module-level array returned directly to the runner; resetConfigureGlobal clears parameters but does not clear that separate plugin registry.

Hypothesis: Sampler.toProperty still identifies properties by an own runBeforeEach field, while PropertyImplem exposes generate/shrink/run without that field. Direct property sampling merits a regression check; worker property classes also retain legacy hook forwarding.

Documentation/configuration drift is visible: custom-reports says verbosity defaults to 1 but readVerbose defaults to None, CONTRIBUTING names Prettier while package.json runs oxfmt, and the core advertises Node >=12.17 while source uses iterator helpers and CI legacy bundles target Node 22.12.

extension_points.summary: Most extension mechanisms are typed APIs and composable factories. Arbitraries define generation and shrinking, plugins wrap execution, and custom RNG factories control randomness. Commands and scheduler hooks adapt testing to stateful or asynchronous systems. Documentation and build configuration provide additional repository-level extension surfaces.

claims.claim: Custom Arbitrary<T> implementations provide generate, canShrinkWithoutContext, and shrink, returning Value objects with context; new public generators are explicitly exported through fast-check.ts.
Arbitrary.filter, map, and chain are composition factories; map accepts an optional unmapper for user-provided values, while chain retains original/chained shrink context and cloned randomness.
Plugin builders receive their execution index and a shared symbol-keyed PluginStore; instances can implement decorateGenerate, decorateRun, onAllRunsComplete, and afterAll.

installGlobalPlugin registers outer wrappers for every runner, while per-call plugins remain local; reporting plugins can throw in onAllRunsComplete to override default assertion reporting, and the older reporter option remains supported.
randomType accepts a seeded generator factory; qualification validates exposed min/max bounds and adapts generators when needed, allowing alternatives to the default xorshift128plus.

Model runners accept user setup functions and iterable commands with check/run behavior; SchedulerImplem accepts a cloneable TaskSelector and act function, with additional customAct wrappers per scheduled task or wait.

Generated objects can expose cloneMethod for repeatable access and toStringMethod/asyncToStringMethod for custom diagnostic serialization; Value and stringify explicitly dispatch through those contracts.

Repository extensions can reuse buildConfigFor with package export mappings; website documentation is discovered through an autogenerated sidebar, and Docusaurus plugins add PWA, TypeDoc, and LLM-readable documentation outputs.

agent_handoff.summary: Tests and CI were inspected, not executed, and this brief is a bounded source inventory rather than an exhaustive audit. Future agents should verify the pinned API and execution contracts before changing generators, plugins, or adapters. Prefer small changes and the existing package/project scripts when implementation and execution are authorized. Publication, destructive packaging, documentation rewriting, and external submission need distinct handling.

claims.claim: Read root/package manifests, pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig.common.json, vitest.config.mjs, and fast-check.ts first; package.json specifies pnpm 12.5.1, and workspace configuration restricts dependency build scripts and enforces release-age/trust policies.

Use this commit's asyncProperty and awaited check/assert contracts; inspect Runner.ts before relying on historical synchronous-property APIs or assuming check cannot throw during parameter qualification/replay.

For arbitrary changes, preserve generation/context/shrink contracts and read the actual colocated ArbitraryAssertions helper; CONTRIBUTING's example still references a historical test/unit location and NextArbitraryAssertions name.

When execution is authorized, start with the root test script in one-shot mode and a relevant --project/file selection, then use applicable typecheck, format:check, and lint:check scripts; tests and CI in this brief were only inspected.

For changes affecting exports or runtime packaging, consult the bundle/type CI jobs: they unpack build artifacts, simulate published contents, run publint and bundle fixtures, and check API extraction plus TypeScript latest/5.8 consumers.

DEFAULT_SEED configures core tests and EXPECT_DEFAULT_SEED can require it; SKIP_DOCUMENTATION bypasses expensive snippet checks, while UPDATE_CODE_SNIPPETS enables Markdown writes. Keep those modes explicit and remember the documentation test evaluates source snippets.

Worker changes require reading main.ts, MainThreadRunner, BasicPool, and generation-mode implementations; use worker assert for cleanup, preserve message runId correlation, and account for disabled shrinking in worker-generated mode.

Treat packaged deletion and release workflows as mutation boundaries; AI_POLICY.md rejects automated external submissions and unreproduced reports/fixes, while CONTRIBUTING requests changesets and scoped gitmoji PR titles for human-owned contributions.
